title: Empirical attention selector slope/backoff tuning and sandboxed regression probe
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Build a sandboxed experiment harness and tuning procedure for the attention kernel selector that focuses on two levers not well-covered by existing prober work: (1) empirical slope estimation for selector confidence (a small-number smoothness prior that reduces oscillation during mode handoffs), and (2) exponential backoff / retry policies for failed or slow kernel activations. The goal is to reduce decode latency spikes and regression incidence during FlashAttention v2->v3 mixed fleets and quantized kernel rollouts while preserving throughput and avoiding overly conservative fallbacks.

Background and motivation: Recent rollouts to enable FlashAttention v3 in the fleet have shown intermittent decode latency spikes for small-batch, long-context requests and occasional kernel selection oscillation under bursty traffic. Existing mitigations (warmup shims, hysteresis windows, and probers) reduce the surface area but are brittle: they either add cold-start overhead or blunt performance gains for the common case. This ticket prototypes an alternative: use short-window empirical slope and variance estimates to smooth probability outputs from the kernel selector and apply a measured backoff/retry strategy when a kernel activation path experiences transient failures or tail latency degradation.

Scope and constraints:
- Sandbox-only: changes should run behind an opt-in canary flag and only in the experiment harness. No infra rollouts until acceptance criteria met.
- Must integrate with existing selector telemetry and per-request tracing (no new heavy-weight tracing).
- Must be safe for multi-tenant Dedicated pools; experiments will run on isolated canary hosts.
- Work focuses on scheduling and decision logic; kernel implementations (FA2/FA3) not modified in this ticket.

Design notes:
1) Slope estimator: compute an exponentially-weighted moving estimate of the selector score gradient over the last N selections (N configurable, default 8). Use slope magnitude + sign to damp instantaneous probability changes: new_prob = mix(prev_prob, raw_prob, alpha = sigmoid(-k * |slope|)). This encourages conservative transitions when the score is changing quickly.
2) Variance-based confidence: combine slope with short-window variance to compute a confidence score; below threshold, inhibit aggressive handoff for 200-500ms.
3) Backoff/retry policy: on detected kernel failure/slow activation (threshold-based on tail latency and error flags), mark kernel as degraded with a configurable initial backoff (e.g., 100ms) and exponential increase up to max_backoff (e.g., 3s). Steps: first failure -> immediate retry on different kernel variant if available; second consecutive failure -> escalate backoff and route requests to fallback for window.
4) Telemetry: emit selector-slope, selector-variance, backoff-state, and backoff-duration tags keyed by host and route. Add a synthetic gauge for handoff oscillation rate (handoffs/sec per 1000 reqs).

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end sandbox runs for 48 hours on canary pool with no production traffic impact.
- 25% reduction in 99.9th pct decode latency spikes attributable to kernel handoffs in the canary compared to baseline (measured by trace-diff).
- Oscillation metric drops by >= 35% compared with current hysteresis-only rollout in the same workload.
- No >3% regression in p50 latency or throughput for steady-state requests.
- Code reviewed and unit+integration tests added for decision logic.
Tasks: Design and implement slope/variance estimators in selector module (config flags)
Implement backoff/retry state machine with in-memory per-host small-state store
Wire telemetry tags and dashboard panels; add alert rule for unexpected backoff growth
Create experiment harness runbook and canary config for isolated Dedicated hosts
Run synthetic workload matrix (see test_plan) and collect baseline vs experiment metrics
Iterate thresholds and k/alpha constants based on empirical results; commit final safe defaults
Prepare PR(s) and coordinate review with runtime and infra owners
Postmortem and decision: either promote to staged canary or iterate further
telemetry_requirements: Selector must emit: selector.slope (float ms-res), selector.variance (float), selector.confidence (float), handoff.oscillation_rate (gauge), backoff.state (enum), backoff.duration_ms (histogram). Ensure tags: host_id, model, route, kernel_variant.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: sandbox on 2 canary hosts (isolated Dedicated pool) for 24h smoke. Stage 1: extended experimental rollout to 20 canary hosts for 48h. Stage 2: gated canary (5% traffic) with automatic rollback if handoff oscillation > baseline*1.2 or backoff-duration 99th > 2x. Promotion subject to acceptance criteria and SRE sign-off.
test_plan: 1) Synthetic matrix: batch sizes [1,2,8,32], seq lengths [512,2048,8192], inter-arrival patterns [steady, bursty]. 2) Failure injection: force kernel activation timeouts and error codes at 0.5%/1% rates. 3) Long-run soak: 48h at production QPS on canary hosts to validate drift. 4) Integration: verify traces contain slope/variance/backoff tags and dashboards report expected reductions.
comments: 2025-03-28 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem review with SRE. Recorded baseline telemetry and initial hypothesis. Adding Marco as assignee for implementation.

2025-03-30 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype slope estimator implemented in selector branch (refs PR wip). Early synthetic runs show reduced oscillation in small-batch tests but slight p50 uplift; investigating smoothing alpha range.

2025-04-01 - Performance review: With alpha=0.2 and k=6, oscillation metric dropped ~40% on synthetic burst tests; p50 increased 1.7% — acceptable within SLA for canary. Action: add variance gating to avoid p50 uplift on steady-state traffic.

2025-04-02 - QA: Added unit tests for slope estimator edge cases (zero-variance input, sparse selections). Integration tests for backoff state machine added; verifying state persistence after host restart.

2025-04-03 - Infra note (SRE - J. Nguyen): Canary hosts provisioned in us-west-2-d; ensure experiment flag set in canary provisioning template. Confirmed no higher than normal error budget consumption overnight.

2025-04-04 - Marco Ruiz: Merged telemetry tags into branch and posted draft PR for review. Next: run 48h sandbox soak and collect canary dashboards for acceptance criteria evaluation. Scheduler owner invited to architecture review.
